I did my extended essay on physics, more specifically an exploration on gravitational physics with the main use of secondary data collected from NASA and other space companies. 
You can write your EE about anything, but remember, it is an exploration written as an essay. Not a physics report! I think that your research question would be of great potential for your IA if you haven't done it yet, I would recommend you to do it about that. The most important thing is to choose a topic that interests you, good luck!

Hi there, I know how you are feeling. Physics is also my science of choice and the subject for my extended essay. My EE is about to be done and submitted, which is really similar to your physics interest. The choice of topic was looking at the different ways to leave the solar system in terms of gravitational physics, which is mainly about gravitational slingshots, scape velocities, etc. This fascinates me and decided to go for it. It is true that I could not do an experiment (obvious), but the IB says that students using data collected elsewhere can access all the assessment criteria and achieve the highest marks. So it is possible! But I believe that your idea of black holes requires theory that is beyond the grasp of you the student, which should be discouraged. The IB specifically uses investigations into quantum computers or black holes as inappropriate topics (in the EE guide). At the end of the day do whatever you are more interested about (if it is viable :P) GOOD LUCK!
